name: noweb
why: Norman Ramsey's literate-programming tool is a small, old, language-agnostic weave-and-tangle design worth an afternoon of curiosity.

brief.what_it_is: noweb is a literate-programming tool in the WEB family: you write one source file that mixes prose and named code chunks, and it produces two outputs. The weave side formats the document for reading (TeX, LaTeX, HTML, or troff back ends). The tangle side extracts the code in compilable order. The homepage says it works with any programming language and uses only 5 control sequences, against WEB's 27. The brew package installs a set of small command-line executables (notangle, noweave, noroots, noindex and others) for these jobs.
brief.why_it_exists: Norman Ramsey built noweb to keep literate programming simple and extensible, and largely language-independent. He says WEB's pretty-printing is the main thing he dropped on purpose, because he finds it distracting while editing and too costly to build per language.
brief.how_it_works: Code is organised into named chunks, written as <<name>> references, and the tangle step expands them into source code. The weave step produces formatted documentation from the same file. The homepage says the design is extensible: new back ends are small (a simpler one can be written in 40 lines of awk, a fuller one in about 250 lines), and customisation can happen without recompiling. Prettyprinting is done by optional filters rather than by the core tool.
brief.install_notes: The brew caveat says TeX support files are installed under $HOMEBREW_CELLAR/noweb/2.13/tex/generic/noweb and may need to be added to TEXINPUTS before noweb's LaTeX output will run. The homepage gives no other setup steps. It mentions Debian packages, CTAN, an RPM attempt, and Jim Pettigrew's Windows 7 instructions using mingw, but none of these is needed on macOS with brew.
brief.standout: The design is deliberately minimal and language-agnostic, and the project makes the case for that in print: the homepage argues for plain-ASCII source over prettyprinted fonts. It has been in use for about thirty-five years and is noted as having been used for tens of thousands of lines across many languages.
brief.status: Maintained, with some caveats. The homepage says the current supported version is 2.12 (28 June 2018), that it moved to GitHub in 2018, and that the copyright runs to 2024. Brew installs 2.13, which is newer than the version the page names, so the homepage may be somewhat behind. The author says Noweb 3 is effectively stuck in alpha and he doubts it will leave that stage, and he advises newcomers to use the 2.x line. I could not see a last-commit date from the homepage.
brief.caveats: The author recommends 2.x over the Noweb 3 alpha. Code is seldom prettyprinted by default. The homepage says no working Emacs mode for noweb existed for Emacs 23 or 24 as of 2012, though the distribution has shipped Thorsten Ohl's noweb-mode since 2.8a. Modified versions may not be called noweb without the author's consent. The TEXINPUTS step is needed for LaTeX output. The homepage describes Lua porting as something it deserves but that will not happen soon.
quotes: Literate programming is the art of preparing programs for human readers.
noweb uses 5 control sequences to WEB's 27.
noweb works "out of the box" with any programming language, and supports TeX, latex, HTML, and troff back ends.
fetch_log: https://www.cs.tufts.edu/~nr/noweb/ : fetched OK. This is a plain HTML home page, not a GitHub repo, and it had enough content that I did not follow further links. It names the GitHub repository as the canonical source, but I did not fetch that URL. Its FAQ, one-page guide, and man pages are linked from it but were not fetched, so commands_seen is empty.

judge.reason: Its tiny, language-agnostic weave-and-tangle workflow is a hands-on introduction to literate programming, an unusual way to make prose and executable code one source.

entry.title: noweb
entry.tldr: A small literate-programming tool: write prose and named code chunks in one file, then weave it into a document or tangle it into compilable source.
entry.deeper_look:
noweb belongs to the WEB family of literate-programming tools. You write a single source file that mixes explanation with named code chunks, referenced as <<name>>. Two programs then read that file. The weave side produces a document for people, with back ends for TeX, LaTeX, HTML and troff. The tangle side expands the chunks and pulls out the code in the order a compiler needs.

Norman Ramsey built it to keep literate programming simple and extensible. It is largely language-independent, and the homepage says it works "out of the box" with any programming language. It uses 5 control sequences where WEB uses 27. Ramsey dropped WEB's pretty-printing on purpose. He finds it distracting while editing and too costly to build for every language, so prettyprinting is left to optional filters.

The idea underneath is the one stated on the homepage: "Literate programming is the art of preparing programs for human readers." The source file is arranged for the reader's understanding, not the compiler's, and the tool reorders it for the machine. The design is also small and open. The homepage says a simple back end can be written in about 40 lines of awk and a fuller one in about 250, so you can read how it works and change it without recompiling anything.

The project is old, around thirty-five years by the homepage's count, and it has been used for tens of thousands of lines of code across many languages.
entry.install:
brew install noweb
# LaTeX output may need the TeX support files on your path:
# add $HOMEBREW_CELLAR/noweb/2.13/tex/generic/noweb to TEXINPUTS
# depends on icon (installed by brew); LaTeX output also needs a TeX installation

try_this.what_happens: Shows the options for the tangle side, which extracts compilable code from a noweb file.
Shows the options for the weave side, which produces TeX, LaTeX, HTML or troff documentation.
Shows how to list the top-level chunks in a noweb file, the ones not referenced by any other chunk.

entry.whats_unique: It is deliberately minimal and language-agnostic, with 5 control sequences, plain-ASCII source, and back ends small enough to write in a few dozen lines of awk.
entry.caveats: The author advises using the 2.x line over the Noweb 3 alpha, code is seldom prettyprinted by default, and LaTeX output needs the TEXINPUTS step.
